borough: London Borough of Barking and Dagenham
decision_conditions: The proposed dwelling, due to its scale, would fail to provide adequately sized double bedrooms or sufficient communal living space for a 2-bedroom, 4-person household, resulting in a cramped and substandard living environment. In addition, the excessively narrow external amenity space would be impractical for household use, further limiting functional living arrangements. Its location would exacerbate this issue by causing overlooking and loss of privacy for No. 17 Ivinghoe Road, resulting in an unacceptable harmful impact on residential amenity. Together, these deficiencies in both internal and external space would significantly reduce the quality of accommodation, making the proposal unacceptable. As such, the proposal is contrary to:DCLG Technical Housing Standards (nationally described space standard) (DCLG, March 2015) (as amended)Policy D6 and Table 3.1 of the London Plan (March 2021)Policy DMD 1 and Part 6 of policy DMNE1 of the London Borough of Barking and Dagenham’s Local Plan (September 2024)Housing Design Standards LPG (June 2023)

The proposed development, due to its bulk, mass, scale, siting, and design, would appear incongruous and fail to integrate with the established character of the area. Its narrow width, inconsistent fenestration, and gabled roof form would disrupt visual cohesion. Additionally, its proximity to the boundary at the entrance to the banjo cul-de-sac would reduce openness at a two-storey level, further impacting the area's character. The proposal is therefore considered unacceptable and contrary to:Paragraphs 131 and 135 of the National Planning Policy Framework (NPPF) (MHCLG, December 2024)Policies D1, D4 and HC1 of the London Plan (March 2021)Policies SP2, SPP6, DMD1 and DMD5 of the London Borough of Barking and Dagenham’s Local Plan (September 2024)

The proposal fails to provide a clear and justified parking strategy, particularly regarding the usability of the proposed off-street parking spaces and the relocation of existing parking. The inconsistency and inaccuracy in the plans leads to uncertainty about the functionality and suitability of the parking provision. The proposed development cannot be accurately assessed and it cannot be demonstrated that it would be supported by the Development Plan. As such, the proposal is considered to be unacceptable and contrary to :National Planning Policy Framework (MHCLG, December 2024)Policy T6 of the London Plan (March 2021)Policy DMT2 of the Barking and Dagenham Local Plan (September 2024)

The proposed development fails to demonstrate that additional demand for parking from the development could be adequately accommodated in the surrounding area. The proposal is therefore likely to add unacceptably to parking stress and congestion in the vicinity of the application site.  As such, it fails to comply with the following policies which seek to ensure proposals show how car parking will be designed and managed and to take into consideration on-street parking availability and existing and planned public transport provision:National Planning Policy Framework (MHCLG, December 2024)Policies T1, T6 and T6.1 of the London Plan (March 2021)Policies DMT1 and DMT2 of the Barking and Dagenham Local Plan (September 2024)
